summary:
MISSION TRACE: Four Minds, One Mission is an interactive, cooperative space mission design game that transforms complex aerospace engineering concepts into an exciting, accessible learning experience.

Inspired by NASA’s systems engineering approach, our game challenges four players to work together as mission specialists to design, launch, and operate a spacecraft exploring potential water-ice deposits near the Moon’s South Pole.

Players must balance engineering constraints such as budget, spacecraft mass, electrical power, and communication capabilities while making decisions under a ten-minute countdown. Each specialist receives a unique responsibility and hidden professional objective, encouraging teamwork, negotiation, and critical thinking. Following launch, players encounter unexpected space emergencies and solve interactive mini-games to keep their mission operational.

Our key innovation is Mission Trace , an in-game analysis system that reveals how engineering decisions influence mission outcomes, helping players understand not only whether their mission succeeded or failed, but why.

By combining gamification, scientific reasoning, and collaborative problem-solving, MISSION TRACE makes space mission engineering more engaging and understandable for students and aspiring space explorers.

Four minds. One mission. Every decision leaves a trace.
details:
MISSION TRACE: Four Minds. One Mission. One Shot at Success.

You have 10 minutes. One spacecraft. Four specialists. And a mission that cannot afford failure.

Would you invest in a more powerful scientific instrument, a stronger communication system, or backup power?

You cannot afford everything. And every choice has consequences.

Welcome to MISSION TRACE, where space exploration is no longer something you simply watch. It's something you design, control, and experience.

The Mission: Explore the Unknown

Your destination? The Moon's South Pole.

Your objective? Design and operate a robotic spacecraft capable of searching for potential signs of lunar water ice.

But there's a catch.

Before your spacecraft even leaves Earth, your team must overcome its first challenge: agreeing on how to build it.

Four players become mission specialists, each responsible for a different part of the mission. Each has a private professional objective, but everyone shares the same goal: mission success.

With just ten minutes on the clock, the team must make critical choices about spacecraft equipment, scientific instruments, power, mass, budget, communications, and mission architecture.

Every upgrade comes with a trade-off. Every second counts.

The Launch Is Only the Beginning

Once the team completes its design, the spacecraft launches into a simulated lunar mission.

Now the real test begins.

Across three orbital sectors, unexpected crises threaten the spacecraft. Communication failures, system malfunctions, and other space hazards force players to think quickly and work together.

Can they restore a damaged system?

Can they protect their scientific data?

Can they keep their spacecraft operational long enough to complete the mission?

Through interactive mini-games, strategic decisions, and cooperative challenges, players discover that a successful mission requires more than the most expensive equipment.

It requires the right decisions, made by the right team, at the right time.

The Twist: Your Decisions Come Back to You

Most games tell you whether you won or lost.

MISSION TRACE tells you WHY.

Our defining innovation is the Mission Trace Report, an interactive post-mission analysis that connects the team's engineering choices, unexpected events, and final outcome.

Imagine discovering that the advanced instrument you selected improved your scientific potential but placed additional demands on your spacecraft's power system.

Or that investing in reliable communications helped your team return valuable discoveries to Earth.

The game turns these connections into understandable feedback, allowing players to learn from both success and failure.

This is where entertainment becomes education.

Built for Curious Minds, Not Rocket Scientists

Inspired by NASA's systems engineering approach, MISSION TRACE introduces real mission-design concepts through simplified, interactive simulations.

Developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, the game runs directly in a web browser, making the experience accessible without specialist equipment.

Our design brings together four essential elements:

  • Mission design: Build a spacecraft within real-world-inspired constraints.
  • Collaboration: Balance four specialists' responsibilities and priorities.
  • Gamification: Explore a randomized lunar map, overcome crises, and solve interactive challenges.
  • Reflection: Discover how decisions shape mission outcomes.

Instead of overwhelming beginners with equations and technical terminology, MISSION TRACE lets them experience engineering principles through visual feedback, experimentation, and teamwork.

Why Does This Matter?

Space missions are built on thousands of interconnected decisions, yet students rarely get the opportunity to experience how those decisions affect one another.

MISSION TRACE changes the way these concepts can be introduced.

It transforms complicated engineering trade-offs into meaningful choices, encourages young people to communicate and collaborate, and shows that failure can be just as valuable for learning as success.

Our ambition is to inspire future scientists, engineers, and explorers by making mission design accessible, memorable, and exciting.

We are not just building a game about space.

We are building a game about the decisions that make space exploration possible.

MISSION TRACE

Four Minds. One Mission. Every Decision Leaves a Trace.
